# Results — Study 13 (Crimson-Hour) on real ES/NQ + SPY/QQQ

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Two tapes: the **faithful**
confluence on **ES=F / NQ=F at 5-minute** fidelity (fine enough to flag IB-high-rejection), and
the **high-power** opening-candle leg on **SPY / QQQ at 1-hour** fidelity (~500 sessions, bars
aligned to the 09:30 open). RTH 09:30–16:00 ET; "red" = close below the 09:30 open. As-of
**2026-06-01**; Yahoo intraday is a rolling window ending ~now, so the start drifts — match the
per-tape fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## ES=F — faithful confluence (44 sessions, baseline red 34.1%)

Conditional **P(session closes red | morning condition)**, with Wilson 95% intervals and the
lift (pp) over baseline:
```
                               k   n   rate  wilson_low  wilson_high  lift_pp
baseline                      15  44 0.3409      0.2188       0.4886   0.0000
oc_red                         9  17 0.5294      0.3096       0.7383  18.8503
oc_green                       6  27 0.2222      0.1061       0.4076 -11.8687
ib_rejected                    7  15 0.4667      0.2481       0.6988  12.5758
ib_not_rejected                8  29 0.2759      0.1470       0.4572  -6.5047
confluence (oc_red & ib_rej)   5  11 0.4545      0.2127       0.7199  11.3636
oc_red & ib_NOT_rej            4   6 0.6667      0.3000       0.9032  32.5758
```

- **The headline cell**: confluence (OC-red & IB-rejected) closed red **5/11 =
  45.5%** — but the Wilson 95% interval is **[21.3%,
  72.0%]** and the Beta(1,1) posterior mean is only **46.2%**
  (95% credible **[21.1%, 72.3%]**). On n=11 the quoted number
  is one draw near the top of a very wide band.
- **Does IB-rejection add anything over OC-red?** Confluence 45.5%
  (5/11) vs OC-red-but-*not*-rejected 66.7%
  (4/6): increment **-21.2 pp**, two-proportion
  z p=**0.40**, Fisher p=**0.62** — indistinguishable. The
  second signal is redundant given the first.

## SPY — opening-candle leg, high power (725 sessions)

P(session closes red | morning condition) — what edgeful quotes:
```
            k    n   rate  wilson_low  wilson_high  lift_pp
baseline  332  725 0.4579      0.4220       0.4943   0.0000
oc_red    237  344 0.6890      0.6382       0.7356  23.1022
oc_green   95  381 0.2493      0.2085       0.2951 -20.8587
```

P(**rest of day** 10:30→16:00 closes red | morning condition) — the part actually unknown at 10:30:
```
            k    n   rate  wilson_low  wilson_high  lift_pp
baseline  320  725 0.4414      0.4056       0.4777   0.0000
oc_red    175  344 0.5087      0.4561       0.5612   6.7342
oc_green  145  381 0.3806      0.3332       0.4303  -6.0802
```

- **Headline** P(session red | OC-red) = **68.9%** (baseline
  45.8%, lift **+23.1 pp**).
- **Genuine forecast** P(rest-of-day red | OC-red) = **50.9%** (baseline
  44.1%, lift **+6.7 pp**).
- **71%** of the headline lift is a *mechanical head-start* (an OC-red day
  is already below its open at 10:30), not continuation. The forecastable edge for the rest of the
  day is the small continuation lift.

## Forking paths — how a mined "confluence" inflates a modest edge

Take the realistic opening-candle edge from the high-power run, **p_true = 70.5%**
(pooled SPY/QQQ P(session red | OC-red)), and let a prompt evaluate **12**
candidate confluences, each measured on edgeful's own **n = 25** sessions. The
*best* observed rate it reports:

- expected best **84.6%** (inflation **+14.1
  pp** over the truth), 95th percentile **92.0%**;
- probability the best reaches edgeful's quoted **88%** by selection alone:
  **36.2%**.

The expected best lands right on the published 88–90%. Selecting the highest of several
tiny-sample confluences manufactures a headline far above the real edge — exactly the "one
prompt, combine the reports until one hits" workflow.
